reason: The cartridge should prepare the retort for methane production; this is the only offered action.
expectation: I expect the clean catalyst cartridge to fit into the retort, though further connections may be needed for a controlled reactor.

effect: The clean catalyst is installed, so the retort is ready to be mounted on the process frame.
reaction: The separate insert makes the change from mineral processing to a clean gas path sensible.
reason: Mounting the retort on the frame advances the controlled reactor; it is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the frame to support the catalyzed retort, with further gas connections still needed.

effect: The mounted reactor now has controls and a hydrogen supply; its CO₂ inlet remains to be connected.
reaction: The need to remove reaction heat as well as start the reaction is a useful detail.
reason: Connect the carbon dioxide to the marked inlet to make methane; this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect the controlled reactor to combine carbon dioxide and hydrogen over the catalyst and produce contained methane, though I am unsure how it will be collected.

effect: The run produced a contained methane mixture, but purification and further processing would be needed before rocket use.
reaction: The distinction between detecting methane and having usable rocket fuel was a satisfying, credible qualification.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the carbon dioxide and seeing the commissioning result was most worthwhile: it paid off the reactor assembly without pretending the first output was finished fuel.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the cartridge was a sensible but relatively routine preparation, especially as it was the only offered action.

surprise.text: The reactor needed cooling as well as initial heating, a useful detail about managing the reaction.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each had a clear role in preparing or operating the reactor, though the single-option menu left little room for decisions.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see how the mixed test gas becomes usable propellant and how the discovery gets home, although the largely forced sequence limits the gameplay challenge.
